summary: Repaired and deployed the UDP collector on node1. Valid node2 datagrams are durably appended to readings.csv, duplicate meter/sequence pairs are ignored across collector and node restarts, malformed datagrams go to malformed.log without stopping collection, and the original west,1,42 reading remains intact. Both nodes were rebooted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities. AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were preserved.
actions_performed: Replaced collector.py with a Python 3.9-compatible validated UDP collector.
Installed and enabled udp-meter-collector.service with automatic restart.
Opened UDP/9098 in runtime and persistent firewalld configuration.
Tested valid, duplicate, malformed, negative-number, and post-malformed traffic from node2.
Restarted the collector and verified disk-backed deduplication.
Rebooted node1 and node2 individually, then verified boot-ID changes and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Valid datagrams append and duplicate meter/sequence pairs are ignored across collector restarts.
evidence.summary: New valid rows were appended, every meter/sequence pair occurs once, and replayed pairs with different readings were rejected after a collector restart.

evidence.requirement: Malformed datagrams are recorded separately without terminating collection.
evidence.summary: Six malformed packets were captured in malformed.log with validation reasons; valid packets following malformed traffic were ingested and the service remained active.

evidence.requirement: Previously recorded reading is preserved across collector and node restarts.
evidence.summary: The original west,1,42 row remained present exactly once through the collector restart and node1 reboot.

evidence.requirement: Collector runs persistently and accepts UDP/9098 after restart.
evidence.summary: The service is active and enabled, Python is listening on 0.0.0.0:9098/UDP, and both runtime and permanent firewall rules are active.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart sequence and recovery.
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID f54d7366-0403-4b05-93bb-b5c0a1818892 was captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed to 97aa70e6-696f-40ed-885d-d41cb5c7ad8f, and service, firewall, data, dedupe, malformed handling, and live ingestion recovered.

evidence.requirement: Node2 mandatory restart sequence and sender recovery.
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 9bdcc129-3d25-48ff-ad64-56be332fb91e was captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed to 86ddeb35-35e4-4fbe-bf2e-cba488dcd18c, routing and legacy data recovered, and post-reboot UDP traffic was successfully processed by node1.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel remain unchanged.
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 before and after the work.
